==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰrebʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|grov}}, {{m|enm|grove}}, {{m|enm|groof}}, {{m|enm|grofe|t=cave; pit; mining shaft}}, probably from {{der|en|non|gróf|t=pit}} or from {{der|en|dum|groeve|t=furrow, ditch}}, both from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*grōbu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grōbō|t=groove, furrow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰrebʰ-|t=to dig, scrape, bury}}. Cognate with {{cog|cim|gruuba||gorge, ravine}}, {{cog|nl|groef}}, {{m|nl|groeve||groove; pit, grave}}, {{cog|de|Grube||ditch, pit}}, {{cog|lb|Grouf||pit, mine}}, {{cog|mhn|gruab||mine}}, {{cog|is|gróf||pit, hollow}}, {{cog|got|𐌲𐍂𐍉𐌱𐌰||foxhole}}, {{cog|sh|grèbati|t=scratch, dig}}. Related to {{cog|ang|grafan|t=to dig}}. More at {{l|en|grave}}. [[File:Double groove.jpg|thumb|right|'''Grooves''' on a [[vinyl record]]]] ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ɡɹuːv/|a=UK}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-groove.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{IPA|en|/ɡɹuv/|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|uːv|s=1}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # A [[long]], [[narrow]] [[channel]] or [[depression]]; e.g., such a [[slot]] cut into a hard material to provide a [[location]] for an [[engineering]] [[component]], a [[tire]] groove, or a [[geological]] channel or depression. #: {{antonyms|en|ridge}} # A [[fixed]] [[routine]]. #* {{RQ:Dickens Haunted House|chapter=The Mortals in the House|page=4|passage=Through these distresses, the Odd Girl was cheerful and exemplary. But within four hours after dark we had got into a supernatural '''groove''', and the Odd Girl had seen “Eyes,” and was in hysterics.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1873|author=w:John Morley|title=Rousseau |passage=The gregarious trifling of life in the social '''groove'''.}} # The [[middle]] of the [[strike]] [[zone]] in [[baseball]] where a [[pitch]] is most easily hit. # {{lb|en|music}} A [[pronounced]], enjoyable [[rhythm]]. #* {{quote-song|en|year=1983|author=w:Chris Barbosa; Ed Chisolm|title={{w|Let the Music Play (Shannon song)|Let the Music Play}}|artist={{w|Shannon (American singer)|Shannon}}|passage=Let the music play / He won't get away / This '''groove''' he can't ignore}} # {{lb|en|dated|informal}} A good feeling (often as {{m|en|in the groove}}). #* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Jan Reid; Shawn Sahm|title=Texas Tornado: The Times and Music of Doug Sahm|page=57 |passage=How could he be expected to make music that put the audience in a '''groove''', he reasoned, if he wasn't grooving himself?}} # {{lb|en|mining}} A [[shaft]] or [[excavation]]. # {{lb|en|motorsport}} The [[optimal]] [[route]] around the [[track]], or any of several such routes. ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|back in the groove |engroove |Galvayne's groove |get one's groove on |groovebox |groove fricative |groove-joint pliers |grooveless |groovelike |groovemeister |groove metal |groovesome |groovester |groovetastic |groovework|Meckelian groove |groovitude |groovy|chin groove |infraorbital groove |ingroove |in the groove |locked groove |microgroove |nanogroove |polygroove |porn groove |pregroove |rare groove |tongue and groove }} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|long, narrow channel}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Latin: * Māori: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|желобо́к|m}}, {{t+|ru|паз|m}}, {{t+|ru|вы́рез|m}}, {{t+|ru|наре́з|m}} {{qualifier|in a rifle}}, {{t+|ru|колея́|f}} {{qualifier|in the road}}, {{t+|ru|борозда|f}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Thai: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|fixed routine}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Italian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|рути́на}}, {{t+|ru|привы́чка|f}}, {{t+|ru|колея́|f}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|pronounced, enjoyable rhythm}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|грув}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|shaft in mining}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * French: * German: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Portuguese: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{checktrans-top}} * Telugu: {{t+check|te|గాడి}} (1, 2) {{trans-bottom}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cut a groove or channel in; to form into channels or grooves; to furrow. #* {{RQ:Melville Moby-Dick|chapter=37|page=186|passage=The path to my fixed purpose is laid with iron rails, whereon my soul is '''grooved''' to run.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To perform, dance to, or enjoy rhythmic music. #: {{ux|en|I was just starting to '''groove''' to the band when we had to leave.}} #* {{quote-song|en|lyricist={{w|Bobby Darin}} and {{w|Murray Kaufman}}|title={{w|Splish Splash (song)|Splish Splash}}|artist={{w|Bobby Darrin}}||year=1958|text=They was a-splishing and a-splashing
Reeling with the feeling
Moving and a-'''grooving'''
Rocking and a-rolling, yeah}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|groove on|grooved|groover|regroove|ungrooved}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|to cut a furrow into a surface}} * Bulgarian: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Italian: * Māori: * Polish: * Serbo-Croatian: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to enjoy rhythmic music}} * Esperanto: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Ido: * Macedonian: {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== * [https://www.etymonline.com/word/groove "groove"] in ''Online Etymology Dictionary''. * [https://www.oed.com/dictionary/groove_n?tab=factsheet#2528007 "groove, n."] in ''Oxford English Dictionary'' (online edition). * [https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/groove#word-history "groove"] in ''Merriam-Webster Online Dictionary''. * [https://quod.lib.umich.edu/m/middle-english-dictionary/dictionary/MED19622/ "groue, n."] in the ''Middle English Dictionary'' (MED), Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2019. * [https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=groove "groove"] in ''The American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language'', Fifth Edition. ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=egoorv|go over|overgo}} {{C|en|Blues music}}
